title: A Alibi for the Portrait
premise: True-crime podcaster Sable Delacroix receives two letters about the thirty-year-old disappearance of painter Vivienne Marsh: one confessing to the crime, one promising the truth is still coming. As Sable investigates, she discovers Vivienne's final portrait depicts a woman who looks exactly like her—and that her own found family of podcast collaborators each hold a fragment of the old alibi. The trail leads back to the coastal town where Sable was raised in foster care, revealing that Vivienne faked her death to escape an abusive patron and has been watching over Sable all along. In the end, Sable must choose between exposing the confession for ratings and protecting the fragile family that chose her, broadcasting a story that frees Vivienne without destroying her.
about_author: Elodie Halloran spent a decade as a court stenographer in small coastal towns before turning to fiction, and her ear for the way people lie on the record infuses every page. She writes from a converted boathouse, where she keeps a wall of unsolved cases she promises herself are research.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Sable Delacroix, mid-recording on her cold-case podcast, opens two letters postmarked the same day: one confessing to the death of painter Vivienne Marsh, one promising 'the rest arrives when you're ready.' POV Sable. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession—the case chooses her before she chooses it.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Frame
chapters.summary: Sable pulls the case file and finds a photograph of Vivienne's last portrait—a woman whose face mirrors her own. Her producer Theo dismisses it as coincidence; archivist June quietly pulls the original auction records. POV Sable. Emotional beat: the chill of recognition, the first crack in her belief that she was never part of any story.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter from Vivienne's 1994 POV: a rising painter trapped by patron Aldous Wren, planning something desperate. Emotional beat: claustrophobic love against duty—Vivienne weighing her art, her safety, and a person she cannot yet name. Ends with her rowing out at night, a canvas wrapped in oilcloth.

chapters.title: Alibi Number One
chapters.summary: Sable interviews retired Sheriff Dane Colter, whose ironclad alibi for the night of the disappearance has never been questioned. He's polished, rehearsed, and lying. POV Sable. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling as she realizes the whole town may be protecting someone—or everyone.

chapters.title: The House That Raised Strangers
chapters.summary: Sable returns to Marrow Bay, the foster town she fled at eighteen, and checks into a boarding house run by Miss Odette, who remembers more than she says. POV Sable. Emotional beat: belonging and dread braided together—home as both wound and refuge.

chapters.title: Letters, Continued
chapters.summary: A third letter arrives, hand-delivered: a sketch of Sable asleep, drawn recently. Someone is close. Theo insists she come home; June sends a digitized page of Vivienne's diary. POV alternating Sable/Theo. Emotional beat: fear for the first time—not for the story, but for herself.

chapters.title: The Patron's Son
chapters.summary: Sable tracks down Julian Wren, Aldous's son, now a dying man in a care home. He hints his father destroyed Vivienne and that the sheriff's alibi was bought. POV Sable. Emotional beat: pity tangled with fury—duty inherited like a disease down the Wren line.

chapters.title: What June Knew
chapters.summary: June reveals she grew up in Marrow Bay too, and that Vivienne once hid a pregnant teenager in her studio—Sable's birth mother. POV June. Emotional beat: found family revealed retroactively; the podcast crew was assembled, unknowingly, around this case.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Lie
chapters.summary: Forensic analysis shows the famous 'last portrait' was painted after Vivienne vanished—an alibi in oils, meant to prove she was alive later than she was. POV Sable. Emotional beat: awe at Vivienne's cunning, and the vertigo of realizing the victim authored the mystery.

chapters.title: The Confessor
chapters.summary: Sable corners the letter-writer: Odette's brother, Emile, the ferryman who took Vivienne across the bay that night. His confession is real—but he confessed to protect someone else. POV Emile then Sable. Emotional beat: guilt as devotion; love expressed through a lifetime of silence.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Theo discovers the statute expires in eleven weeks; whatever happens, the legal window is closing fast, and a rival true-crime outlet smells blood. POV Theo. Emotional beat: pressure and loyalty in conflict—he wants to protect Sable even if it costs the story.

chapters.title: Aldous Wren's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the Wren estate archives, Sable finds a ledger of payments—to the sheriff, to the coroner, to a maternity home. The last entry is dated nine months before her own birth. POV Sable. Emotional beat: the floor drops out; her origin and the crime are the same event.

chapters.title: The Mother Question
chapters.summary: Sable confronts June: was her birth mother the girl Vivienne hid? June gives her a sealed letter Vivienne left 'for the child, if she ever asks.' Sable can't open it yet. POV Sable. Emotional beat: grief deferred; the weight of a question she isn't ready to survive answering.

chapters.title: Someone Follows the Signal
chapters.summary: Sable's hotel room is searched; her recording equipment tampered with. A figure on the cliff road at night. She realizes the second letter-writer—the promiser—is not Emile. POV Sable. Emotional beat: hunted; the investigation turns inside out, and trust becomes a liability.

chapters.title: The Second Hand
chapters.summary: Trap set with Theo and June, they catch the follower: Dane Colter's daughter, Lena, a private investigator hired years ago by someone paying monthly to keep watch on 'the girl from the studio'—Sable. POV Lena. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; another orphan folded into the circle.

chapters.title: The Island Studio
chapters.summary: Following Lena's payment trail to a defunct account, Sable crosses to Gullwrack Island and finds a hidden cottage: fresh paint, canvases, a life half-lived. Someone has been here within days. POV Sable. Emotional beat: trembling hope—the dead woman may be alive, and waiting.

chapters.title: Vivienne
chapters.summary: The reunion: Vivienne Marsh, older, wary, alive. She explains the faked death, the purchased alibis, and why she watched over Sable—her best friend's daughter, the child she promised to guard. POV Vivienne. Emotional beat: love against duty made flesh; thirty years of protection mistaken for haunting.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Vivienne will surrender only if the confession clears Emile and names Aldous Wren's crimes without exposing the living network that sheltered her—including Odette, June's family, and Sable's mother. Sable must decide what the story owes the people in it. POV Sable. Emotional beat: the ethics of narrative; duty to truth versus duty to people.

chapters.title: Deadline at the Sheriff's Door
chapters.summary: With four days left on the statute, Sable confronts Dane Colter with the ledger and recordings. He breaks—not out of shame, but because his daughter stands beside the woman he helped bury. POV Dane. Emotional beat: collapse of a bought conscience; the alibi finally unravels aloud.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: The finale episode airs: Emile exonerated, Wren's crimes documented, Vivienne legally declared alive under a protected identity negotiated off-record. Sable holds back the parts that would destroy her found family. POV Sable. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by cost; a story told honestly and mercifully at once.

chapters.title: The Letter She Finally Opens
chapters.summary: Alone at dawn, Sable reads Vivienne's sealed letter from her mother—a message of love, apology, and permission to belong wherever she is loved. She weeps, then laughs, then calls Theo and June. POV Sable. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude fused; the found family confirmed as real family.

chapters.title: A Portrait, Signed
chapters.summary: On Gullwrack, Vivienne paints Sable at last—this time from life, sitting across the easel. The podcast ends its run; a new one begins, about the ones who survived. POV Sable, closing frame mirroring chapter one. Emotional beat: belonging complete; the coldest case closed warm.
